builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TeCoP: Accelerating Diffusion Large Language Model Decoding via Tentative Context Pipelining
summary: TeCoP replaces the serialized block-wise decoder of diffusion LLMs (LLaDA, Dream) with a training-free staggered block-parallel pipeline that reuses stable but uncommitted predictions as provisional context, committing them via confidence and stability checks in a draft-and-verify loop. It costs implementation complexity in the decoding loop and carries the accuracy risk of committing tokens conditioned on provisional context that later proves wrong, though reported accuracy stays within one point of the original decoder. It can fail on workloads where low-confidence or unstable early predictions propagate errors across blocks, and it applies only to diffusion LLMs, not autoregressive models.
rationale: The speedup is large, training-free, and fits a single 24GB GPU, but it only benefits teams already serving diffusion LLMs, so its value must be validated against the reader's actual model stack and accuracy tolerance.
technique: Tentative context pipelining for diffusion LLM decoding

claims.statement: TeCoP replaces the serialized block-wise decoder of diffusion LLMs (LLaDA, Dream) with a training-free staggered block-parallel pipeline that reuses stable but uncommitted predictions as provisional context, committing them via confidence and stability checks in a draft-and-verify loop. It costs implementation complexity in the decoding loop and carries the accuracy risk of committing tokens conditioned on provisional context that later proves wrong, though reported accuracy stays within one point of the original decoder. It can fail on workloads where low-confidence or unstable early predictions propagate errors across blocks, and it applies only to diffusion LLMs, not autoregressive models.

Up to 87% fewer forward evaluations and up to 7.50x throughput without KV caching (11.77x with caching) over the uncached original decoder, with average cached accuracy within one percentage point of the original.
